subject: PoC mode clarification + stakeholder gaps for Healthlyt trial
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC mode clarification + stakeholder gaps for Healthlyt trial

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Call summary:
- Primary ask: validate inference latency, throughput and quality on the clinical triage model across ~100k daily predictions.
- Compliance: production must be in a Private VPC (PHI). For the PoC you can provide a de-identified dataset, but you flagged a later cutover requirement to VPC.
- Preference: your ML team is open to an initial Hosted trial for fast iteration, but Engineering needs clarity on resource isolation and throughput (Dedicated vs Private for production).

Proposed PoC structure (from Redwood):
1) Phase A (Host-friendly, 2 weeks): Hosted API with a de-identified sample — validate correctness, functional integration, and initial latency targets.
2) Phase B (Dedicated-prototype, 4 weeks): Reserved capacity replica to validate steady-state throughput and autoscaling behavior with near-production load.
3) Phase C (Pre-prod VPC dry run, optional): network and KMS integration to confirm private deployment readiness.

Success criteria (draft, attached): see MVP_success_criteria.xlsx — short list: 95th pct latency < 350ms for typical requests, sustained throughput 2k req/min with <1.5x cost multiplier vs baseline, no tokenization/regression failures across the 10 golden prompts.

Questions / asks for Healthlyt:
- Confirm who will be the owning stakeholders for: ML validation (Emma), infra/security (procurement@healthlyt.com or IT), and legal for the SOW.
- Can you confirm whether the de-identified dataset is ready by Aug 9?
- Any constraints on running a Dedicated trial inside your cloud account vs Redwood-managed Dedicated? (Rohit from Cloud Partner may weigh in.)

Attachments: MVP_success_criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet with proposed pass/fail checks).

If that looks correct I can circulate a short SOW draft and book a kickoff for the week of Aug 9.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.ai

Thanks Avery — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can deliver a de-identified dataset by Aug 6 (not Aug 9) — abundance of caution on dates.
- Confirming: production must be Private VPC with KMS-managed keys; however, we are comfortable with a Hosted Phase A as long as the data is de-identified and we have a clear path to move to VPC.
- We need concrete throughput numbers for Dedicated (what instance types and expected concurrency do you recommend for ~2k req/min?). Can Karthik propose a sizing estimate?

Looping in Rohit to advise on whether Healthlyt's cloud environment can host a Redwood Dedicated pool (we may prefer Redwood-managed Dedicated first, then a lift-and-shift later).

Emma Liu

Thanks — quick engineering read and proposed runbook: 

Sizing & runbook:
- For the Dedicated phase to hit ~2k req/min with 95th pct latency targets, we recommend starting with a 2x A100-equivalent GPU pool (or equivalent G4dn-16xlarge-like config) with continuous batching and per-request concurrency tuned to the model size (we'll confirm exact vCPU/GPU mapping after model artifact review).
- Phase A (Hosted) objective: integration, latency baselining, and quality gating with the de-id dataset. Use continuous batching with a small KV cache window to simulate production prefix reuse.
- Phase B (Dedicated): load test to steady state (3x expected peak for safety) and validate autoscale/fallback behavior. We'll provision metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, cost per 1M tokens.

Success criteria (engineering):
- p95 latency < 350ms on requested payload distribution (matches Avery's doc).
- No tokenization failures on the 10 golden prompts.
- Sustained throughput >= 2k req/min for 30 continuous minutes without error spikes.

Timeline suggestion:
- Week 0-1: kickoff, data transfer (de-id set), initial Hosted tests.
- Week 2-3: iterate, baseline, share results + RSVP decision for Dedicated phase.
- Week 4-6: Dedicated runbook, autoscale verification, security dry-run.

I attached a short SOW draft that reflects the split-phase approach (SOW-Healthlyt-draft.docx). Please review and flag any legal/procurement items.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
